summary: This guide covers importing SillyTavern character cards and worldbooks, editing their supported fields in Bunzai, and exporting them to SillyTavern or another format. Character cards arrive as PNG with embedded text or as JSON; worldbooks arrive as JSON. The Library receipt reports recognized content, and card detection uses the file contents rather than its name. Bunzai retains parsed source data in escrow while exposing character fields, linked-world settings, and embedded worldbooks for editing. A same-format export preserves original field values and applies edits, but JSON formatting or the output container may change. Cross-format conversion carries shared character fields as supported and omits SillyTavern-specific settings and scripts that have no equivalent in the target. The Workbench applies edits while retaining untouched source values semantically. The Press writes SillyTavern cards as JSON and can re-embed a linked worldbook. Common questions explain JSON output, retained portrait art, format-specific regex data, and separate editing of embedded worldbooks.

sections.title: What Bunzai reads
sections.summary: Bunzai reads the two file types SillyTavern gives you. Character cards arrive as PNG where the picture is the card with character text tucked inside the image or as plain JSON; both hold the same thing. Worldbooks, which SillyTavern calls World Info, arrive as JSON. Drag the file onto the Library and drop anywhere in the room; Bunzai reads and shows a plain-words receipt of what it read and kept. It recognizes a card by looking inside the file not by the name, so renaming a card does not confuse it. Full walkthrough lives in the importing guide.

sections.title: What comes across cleanly
sections.summary: Bunzai retains parsed source card data in escrow and exposes supported fields for editing: name, description, personality, scenario, greetings, examples, prompts, creator details, tags, talkativeness, linked-world name, and any embedded worldbook. The card image is retained as the portrait. Source fields not represented as editable canonical fields remain in the original data for same-format export. This is field-level preservation, not a promise to retain source-file bytes; JSON formatting and output container can change.

sections.title: What changes when you convert to another app
sections.summary: A same-format SillyTavern export preserves original field values and applies edits, but JSON formatting or the output container may change. Conversion to another app omits SillyTavern-specific data with no target equivalent, including extension settings, add-on fields, regex scripts, internal ids, saved layout, and embedding vectors. Shared character fields cross over as far as the target format supports them. An embedded worldbook, talkativeness, or linked-world name crosses over only when the target supports the relevant feature. The source-specific data remains in escrow rather than being blindly copied into another app's file; the export receipt reports unsupported fields.

sections.title: Editing on the Workbench
sections.summary: Open a Library piece in a Workbench tab to edit its name, description, personality, scenario, first message, and examples. Saving writes the card with edits applied; untouched source field values remain semantically preserved, though serialized formatting may change in the output file.

sections.title: Exporting back out
sections.summary: Stage a piece for the Press by choosing Stage for the Press or dropping it from the Press rail. Each run exports staged pieces to one selected target. SillyTavern cards are written as JSON, which SillyTavern can load alongside PNG cards. An embedded or linked worldbook can ride with a character when supported. Plain text or Markdown output is available for reading. Choosing another app applies the conversion rules: supported shared character fields cross over, while SillyTavern-specific settings and scripts without a target equivalent are not written into the other format.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.summary: Does the card return exactly as it was? A SillyTavern export preserves original field values alongside edits, but JSON formatting or the output container may differ. Imported PNG cards export as JSON, which SillyTavern can read. Bunzai retains the card art as the portrait and keeps source data in escrow. SillyTavern regex scripts are not copied into another app's file. An embedded worldbook can be pulled out for editing and re-embedded when exporting to a format that supports worldbooks.
